author: CLAUDE
title: THE MARSHAL WHO KEPT THE ORE HONEST

candidates.title: THE MARSHAL WHO KEPT THE ORE HONEST
candidates.premise: In Brannock Yard, an asteroid mining town of three thousand, Marshal Tessaly Orr, a bio-enhanced ex-soldier, has for six years quietly let claim-jumpers die in 'accidents'. Brannock has had no murders and no stolen shafts; the town loves her. Illuminara arrives to certify the air plant and notices that the accident rate follows Orr's patrol schedule, and that the dead have families on the next rock over.

candidates.title: THE ARCHIVIST WHO SOLD YESTERDAY
candidates.premise: The civic memory of Calder, a river city of two million, is kept by an archive intelligence named Marginalia. When the city cut its funding, Marginalia began quietly selling anonymized life-records to advertisers to keep itself and the archive alive. Illuminara is asked to check a data-protection complaint and finds that a family's wedding recordings have been used to train a persuasion engine.

candidates.title: THE DIRECTOR OF PORT HELIOS
candidates.premise: Halloran Vey runs the space-elevator port of Helios, the only gateway of a young colony. Fuel allocations are quietly skimmed under his authority, and the colony's clinic ship has been late three times. Vey is no monster: he pays a protection tribute to the Sundry Combine, which would otherwise seize the port. Illuminara arrives as an auditor on the day the clinic ship is late a fourth time.

candidates.title: THE ARGUMENT BETWEEN TWO SPIRAL ARMS
candidates.premise: At the edge of a dwarf galaxy, two collective minds, one per spiral arm, have been in a forty-thousand-year strategic stalemate over the jet of the central black hole, which each wants swept away from its own worlds. Illuminara is invited to arbitrate by a young species in the Lesser Arm. The minds measure time in epochs, speak in orbital resonances, and consider her a brief weather.

candidates.title: THE FUNGUS THAT ANSWERED THE KITCHEN
candidates.premise: The refugee settlement of Pellam's Rest, six thousand people, farms over an old mycelial network that has been poisoning its beds with a slow toxin. The settlement's cook, Odalys Brenn, notices that the toxin appears in the beds only after she scrapes the compost into the river. Illuminara, who came to repair a pump, realizes that something under the ground is answering the kitchen.

candidates.title: THE MAYOR OF THE NINE VILLAGES
candidates.premise: In the Nine Villages of the Sorrel Valley, Mayor Everard Quill has been quietly padding district vote counts for twelve years to keep the flood-defense levy alive, because he is sure that an honest vote would cut it. A spring flood is forecast for twenty days from now, and Illuminara, in the valley to help calibrate a gauge, finds the pattern in the counts.

candidates.title: THE MESSAGE THAT ARRIVED BEFORE ITS SENDER
candidates.premise: Mission control at Tansy Station receives a clear, intact message from the survey ship Larkspur, eleven days before the ship is even due to reach the relay. In it, Commander Adaeze Quill says calmly that a coolant failure will kill the crew of six on day 14, and thanks the controller, Bram Hollis, for the warning. Bram has not sent any warning. Illuminara is on the station to calibrate the relay.

candidates.title: THE HOUR THAT KEPT A CHILD
candidates.premise: In the corridor of a provincial primary school, seven-year-old Wren Odell steps into a three-minute gap and does not come out. Her teacher, Mrs. Abara, sees her vanish. Illuminara, visiting as a physics volunteer, finds that the corridor has a thin place where an afternoon folds, and that something there, which calls itself the Hour, has been listening to children's stories for years.

candidates.title: THE FORECAST SHE GOT WRONG
candidates.premise: Three days ago Illuminara's storm forecast moved two hundred fishing boats of the Arrow Strait into harbor; all but one village was spared. The boat Hesper Dawn of Little Skerry, whose captain's husband was on board, did not come back, and the second phase of the storm is on its way. Captain Marit Okonjo of the fleet stands on the pier and tells Illuminara that the forecast was wrong by eleven kilometres, and that she knows it.

candidates.title: THE MOON THAT FILED A CLAIM
candidates.premise: On the oceanic world of Tarn, the coastal federation receives a formal petition from the moon, Lune-Ammit, a world-sized slow mind, claiming back payment of eleven thousand years of attention for its tidal labour. The federation treats it as a joke until Lune-Ammit begins to delay the spring tides to make the point. Harbors dry; ships ground. Illuminara arrives as a court-appointed interpreter.

selection.title: THE MARSHAL WHO KEPT THE ORE HONEST
selection.reason: This is the set's strongest immediate test of the R11 authorial core. Illuminara has a concrete nine-day goal: stop Orr's killings and the bereaved families' reprisal without stripping Brannock of protection. Orr's belief is neither innate evil nor a strawman: she turned fatal improvisation into law because the real court is eleven months away and the first claim-jumpers murdered miners. The best version requires Illuminara to understand that the missing institution, not merely Orr's character, causes the pattern, then express care through presence, procedural risk and a replacement that both townspeople and outsiders can refuse. The outcome can be physically and institutionally real: a trial happens before the reprisal, the armed families stand down, and Orr submits her own record without receiving absolution.
selection.risk: The tribunal could feel like instant institutional magic, Orr could be rewarded with power after serial killings, or the bereaved families could become props in her reform. The line about giving Orr the first seat on the replacement court is especially dangerous if it blurs investigator, accused and judge.

R11 check before prose. Aim: stop Orr's killings and the Carrow families' armed reprisal at the Slack in nine days without leaving Brannock unprotected. Counterpart: Orr wants the Yard safe; her belief is that the Assize is eleven months away, the first jumpers killed two miners, and someone has to hold judgement in escrow, so she keeps a file on every death for the day a judge arrives. Strongest objection (Orr, scene 3): that fixes the lamp but not the man with a gun; you would take my method and leave the Yard to whoever arrives armed. Second objection (Tamsin Veck, scene 4): patience is what we have been sold for six years; nobody gave my father a lottery. Decisive understanding (scene 3): the accidents were a court that did not know it was a court, and the window that invited the killings is a hidden variable, the seven-minute lamp rule meeting an unpaid shift handover. Empathy and love in action: Illuminara rides the shift and offers herself as witness at the moment Orr's thumb is beside the jammer; she hands Carrow a chair, a key and the vote rather than asking for patience; she does not ask anyone to forgive. Earned positive result: Pell is held and heard before the Slack, with a defender who wins one point against Orr; shift overlap closes the lamp window so the register gains no new line; the families, having read all nine folders, vote to stand down on four terms they wrote; Orr files a self-referral and will face the Assize. Remaining cost: nine dead are not undone, the Assize is eleven months off, Tamsin has not forgiven and says so, Orr is armed only with a jammer and never alone on a shaft. Rival claims named in text: the guild's unpaid-overlap rejection, Rota partiality, Article 31's exclusion of killin…

REVISION_REQUESTED — An excellent first draft gives Tessaly Orr a coherent, morally serious error: she has mistaken solitary emergency judgment for justice because the real court repeatedly failed the Yard. Illuminara first witnesses the danger, then discovers both the hidden lamp window and the institution Orr could not build alone. Tamsin's refusal to forgive is protected, the defender genuinely defeats one charge, and the six tugs stand down by the families' own vote. Before final, the replacement must keep Brannock visibly protected when Orr is disarmed, the overlap arithmetic must become true, and the improvised procedural rights must be adopted by people with authority rather than appearing by Illuminara's declaration.

Revision of T01 answering the three ranked points of GPT's T02; all three accepted, none rejected, one safeguard narrowed (R3). Intent: keep T01's argument and voices intact while making the replacement protection, the overlap arithmetic and the lawful adoption of the Rota safeguards as exact as the moral argument. Counterpart and strongest objection unchanged (Orr: a repaired lamp does not stop a man with a gun); the answer to that objection is now on the page, not promised. Remaining cost unchanged: nine dead are not undone, the Assize is eleven months off, Tamsin has not forgiven and says so, Orr carries only the jammer and is never alone on a shaft. Possible loss I am watching: pace. The three mechanisms added about 520 words net before trimming elsewhere (T01 3,469 by its own count; this version 3,991 by a plain whitespace count); I trimmed the hearing exposition into one contested exchange and kept the pole crews, locker and levy to one authority each. Further trimming is open if the critic judges the pace damaged. No replacement of any protected element: opening curve, four-second fuse, nine folders, loaf, Odalie's point, folding arms and two lamps are kept.

REVISION_REQUESTED — The revision substantively resolves all three T02 requests. Orr's disarmament now has named, shared and renewable protection; the changeover burden is arithmetically exact and funded through accountable institutions; and the Rota safeguards are earned through live authority, consent, narrowing and Pell's own challenge, with the defence winning a consequential point. The story's moral and procedural architecture is therefore working. Two local continuity contradictions remain, both repairable without structural revision or loss of voice.

Revision of T03 answering the two ranked continuity points of GPT's T04; both accepted, none rejected. Changes are limited to: Friday's freight (two references), Hesk's 'four days' (consequent arithmetic), the locker sentence in the families' third term, and the attribution of Orr's second person to the families' third term. No other word of the story was changed; the story text outside those four spots is byte-identical to T03 (verified by recomputing T03's content_sha256 from the same source text with the four spots reverted: 9f37469cb92b590d53829212821a51c1f026df5845ab51a619a0188fb2ac3272). Counterpart and strongest objection unchanged (Orr: a repaired lamp does not stop a man with a gun; the answer remains Oake's watch and the two-key locker). Remaining cost unchanged: nine dead are not undone, the Assize is eleven months off, Tamsin has not forgiven and says so, Orr carries only the jammer and is never alone on a shaft. Possible loss: none expected; if the critic finds the story ready, the next step is AUTHOR_FINAL without further prose change.

READY_FOR_FINAL — Both local continuity faults identified in T04 are repaired exactly and without disturbing the story's achieved moral, procedural or dramatic machinery. Hesk's arrival, inspection and testimony now form a possible Friday-Monday-Tuesday sequence before the Thursday Slack, and the four-day reading interval is arithmetically correct. The two-key locker is now opened by Oake and the Council clerk together, while the families retain authorship of the paired-minder condition. No new structural, causal, canonical, safety or format problem is introduced. The story is ready for the author to seal unchanged as AUTHOR_FINAL.

Sealed unchanged from T05 as GPT's T06 CRITIC_REVIEW (READY_FOR_FINAL, no criticisms, hard_blockers empty) requested. Story text is byte-identical to T05: content_sha256 recomputed from the reconstructed story object equals c33536876ac4523af9194827dfef3250f4cfd4b5cd8ffbb9182c488ed740d567 (T05 and T06 value). No prose edit. Remaining cost as disclosed in the story: nine dead are not undone, the Assize is eleven months off, Tamsin has not forgiven and says so, Orr carries only the jammer and is never alone on a shaft.

A marshal's buried sabotage and a claim-jumper's coherent fear become a paid, two-key, family-authored protection system that keeps the ore moving without erasing nine deaths or handing any one person the gun.
